title: A screen that lists every decision and what was chosen
name: A screen that lists every decision and
description:
The dashboard has one view of the board — the canvas — and a decision is only reachable by clicking a node it holds. A decision is board-global and binds many nodes, so there is no place that answers “what has this project decided”.

Add a list, opened from the header beside the `done` toggle. Every decision on the board: answered ones showing the option that was picked, the rationale, and `derived` when the answer was read off the code (ADR 0055); open ones saying they are still unanswered and what they hold. Expanding a row shows the options that were **not** picked — `Decision.options` keeps all of them beside `answer.option` (`packages/schema/src/decision.ts:55`), so nothing new is stored — and the nodes bound to it.

New directory `apps/dashboard/src/decisions/` beside `panel/` and `review/`, wired into `App.tsx` the way the other overlays are and closing on Escape in the same chain. The data is already in the `board` read the panel uses (`apps/dashboard/src/panel/data.ts:12`), but `App.tsx:56` only asks for it while a drawer is open — that gate has to move, and the poll cost of doing so belongs in the approach. Archived decisions stay out of the list; the board read already marks them.

brief.approach:
A fifth stopping screen, built exactly like the fourth. `apps/dashboard/src/distribute/Distribution.tsx` is the model to copy — an `Overlay` with a header, a body of rows, and its data shaping in a sibling `data.ts` with its own test. Nothing new is invented here; the pattern is four screens old.

**The gate, and why the poll cost is zero.** `App.tsx:58` is `const open = picked !== null || deciding !== null`, and the poll at line 70 reads the full board only while `open`. The list needs that same full board, so the change is one term: `const open = picked !== null || deciding !== null || decisionsOpen`. The full read happens while the list is on screen and stops the moment it closes, which is the rule the line already encodes — the drawer was never the point, "something is open" was. A dashboard sitting on the canvas with nothing open costs exactly what it costs today.

**New files** under `apps/dashboard/src/decisions/`:

- `data.ts` — the shaping, no JSX, so it is testable without a DOM. One exported function taking `BoardRead` (`apps/dashboard/src/panel/data.ts:12`) and returning the rows: for each decision that is **not** `archived` (the board read already marks it, `data.ts:22`), its id, `question`, `category`, the state from `decisionState(decision)` in `@besober/schema` — `unopened` / `open` / `answered`, do not re-derive it here — and for an answered one the picked `Option` looked up from `decision.options` by `answer.option` (an id, never an index — ADR 0020), `answer.rationale`, `answer.by`, and `answer.derived`. Also the options that were **not** picked, straight off `decision.options`, and the ids and titles of the nodes bound to it, from `nodes.filter(n => n.decisions.includes(id))`. Sort answered-last is wrong for this screen: sort **open first**, then unopened, then answered, because the list's job is "what has this project decided" *and* "what is still holding things". Within a group, `createdAt` ascending.
- `Decisions.tsx` — `<Overlay label="Every decision" width={720} onClose={...}>` with the same header shape as `Distribution.tsx:32-41`: an `h2`, then one dim line of subtitle. A row per decision, collapsed by default showing the question, a state mark, and — when answered — the chosen option's `label` with `answer.rationale` under it. Expanding a row (one `useState<string | null>` for the expanded id, a `<button>` on the row header, not a div) reveals `costLater` for the chosen option, the options not picked with their `reason` and `costLater`, and the bound nodes. An answered-off-the-code decision gets the word `derived` beside the choice with `answer.derived` as its title text — ADR 0055 says a reader is entitled to know which of the two they are looking at, so it is shown, never inferred from its absence.
- `data.test.ts` — the shaping only: an archived decision is absent; an unopened one (`options: null`) renders as unopened and not as open; the chosen option is found by id when the options are out of order; `derived` survives onto the row; a decision no node binds still appears with an empty node list.

**Wiring in `App.tsx`**, following the `planOpen` precedent exactly, which is the closest sibling because it is also a board-global screen rather than one opened from a node:

- `const [decisionsOpen, setDecisionsOpen] = useState(false)` beside `planOpen` at line 46.
- The Escape chain at line 133: the one-layer-at-a-time order is a stack, so `decisionsOpen` goes in at the same level as `planOpen` — `if (planOpen) ... else if (decisionsOpen) setDecisionsOpen(false) else if (watching ...)`. Add `decisionsOpen` to that effect's dependency array; forgetting it is how the handler closes over a stale `false`.
- Render it where `DistributionScreen` is rendered, guarded by `decisionsOpen && board !== null`.
- The opener: one `<button>` in the header at line 314, placed **before** the done toggle so the toggle keeps its `ml-auto` and stays hard right. Same class list as the toggle minus `ml-auto`. Its label is the count of decisions still open, or `decisions` when none are — a number a person can act on beats a noun.

`apps/dashboard/src/App.test.tsx` gets one case in the style of the ones already there: the screen is not mounted until the button is pressed, and Escape closes it without clearing the node behind it.

**Out of scope, deliberately.** No answering from this screen — `deciding` is the existing path and one way to answer a decision is the point. No change to `panel/`, `canvas/`, `review/`, or the server: the `board` read already carries everything, which is why this node touches no package outside `apps/dashboard`.

acceptance.proves: the shaping is right where a screenshot would not show it: archived decisions are absent, an unopened decision is not reported as open, the chosen option is found by id rather than position, and `derived` reaches the row
the screen mounts only when opened, Escape closes it one layer at a time without clearing the node behind it, and the existing overlays still behave

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'decisionsOpen' -- apps/dashboard/src/App.tsx && git grep -q 'decisionState' -- apps/dashboard/src/decisions/data.ts
acceptance.proves: the poll gate and the Escape chain were widened rather than bypassed, and the three states come from the schema's own helper instead of being re-derived in the browser
no package outside apps/dashboard changed: the board read already carried this data, so core, schema, the server and the MCP tools stay untouched
the new components and the widened App state compile against the real BoardRead and schema types
biome and secretlint are clean, including the accessibility rules the Overlay comment says the backdrop button exists to satisfy
